PullRequest.Title: eslint: fix bracket notation in remote tooling
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- replace bracket notation with dot notation for identifier-like properties in the Remote, tunnels, networking, and authentication cleanup group
- remove all 11 cleaned paths in that group from `.eslint-allowed-bracket-notation-files`
- replace private-member access in the GitHub authentication test with an explicit persisted-session reader seam
- exercise remote tunnel startup through its registered public command instead of calling a private contribution method

This PR is intentionally stacked on #334756, which enables `local/code-no-bracket-notation-for-identifiers`. Its base should be changed to `main` after #334756 merges.

## Validation

- targeted ESLint with `--max-warnings=0` across all changed JavaScript and TypeScript files
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- targeted compilation of the GitHub and Microsoft authentication extensions
- `npm run transpile-client`
- focused core unit tests — 70 tests passed
- focused GitHub authentication integration test — 1 test passed
- targeted hygiene across all 13 changed files
- `git diff --check`

Scenarios.Scenario: Microsoft authentication experimentation initialization during extension activation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The experimentation service waits for its existing initializePromise and initialFetch before returning; the changed packageJSON version lookup occurs before those existing waits and adds no work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Experimentation service initialization and initial treatment fetch performed by vscode-tas-client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initialization/fetch sequence per created experimentation service; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same service was created with the same extension version and awaited the same initialization/fetch promises.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both promises are awaited on the service creation path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Service creation frequency, normally extension activation rather than per request; unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two existing awaits remain serialized; no concurrency change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The external service/global state controls treatment caching; the diff does not alter keys, state, initialization, or cold/warm behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: bracket and dot access target the identical own property name `version`.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External fetch duration varies, but it is entirely pre-existing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; the diff does not add, repeat, or move the network work.

Scenarios.Scenario: GitHub authenticated asset download, including redirects
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each download awaits fetch and bounded response reading; redirect handling can issue another request before completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authenticated GitHub GET and any manual redirect follow-ups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request plus at most the existing maximumRedirects follow-ups per logical download.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Authorization header was assigned to the same key before each authenticated request using bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Network responses and body reading are on the download critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Logical downloads and redirect count; neither changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing transport queue/rate limiter behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Requests remain `cache: no-store`; no key, coalescing, or cache lifecycle changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: `headers.Authorization` and `headers['Authorization']` perform the same property assignment.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Download sizes and network latency vary but are unaffected.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; request count, bytes, scheduling, and authorization behavior are unchanged.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: On the first uncached check, Windows version detection precedes either `wsl.exe --status` or a filesystem stat; subsequent calls reuse the memoized promise unless refresh is requested.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one per memoized cold check, plus explicit refresh calls; unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same executable path was derived from the same SystemRoot environment property.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat lxss/LxssManager.dll on older Windows builds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one per memoized cold check on the older-build branch; unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same DLL path was derived from the same SystemRoot environment property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The stat is awaited before returning feature availability.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cold checks and explicit refresh calls, not environment property access syntax.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent warm callers share the same promise; explicit refresh can replace it as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing module-level promise still coalesces warm calls; refresh semantics are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: dot and bracket access both read `process.env` key `SystemRoot`.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Subprocess duration varies by host, but no changed mechanism reaches it more often.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; subprocess/filesystem cardinality and memoization remain identical.

Scenarios.Scenario: Node HTTP request with retries and redirects
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A request attempt awaits the network response; qualifying redirects recursively issue the existing follow-up request, and transient idempotent failures can retry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Node HTTP(S) request, redirect follow-ups, and transient retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing bound of up to three attempts, with the existing redirect budget per request chain; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Location header was tested and read from the same lower-case `location` property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All requests needed for a successful response are on the caller's critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Redirect depth and transient retry count, both bounded and unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Redirects and retries remain sequential; independent callers retain their existing concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The optional no-store request setting and all cache behavior remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both syntaxes read the identical `location` key on IncomingHttpHeaders.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network latency is variable, but no extra request is introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; redirect detection and network cardinality are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: HTTP and CONNECT traffic through TunnelProxy
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each incoming proxy request parses its destination and either forwards via `http.request` or establishes/reuses a tunnel socket; header filtering precedes forwarding.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward plain HTTP requests through the shared tunnel agent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One forwarding request per incoming HTTP request; tunnel sockets remain pooled by host and port.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same connection, te, and upgrade keys were read/deleted before forwarding.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Header filtering is synchronous and the network response is on the proxied request critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a remote tunnel socket for CONNECT traffic when no reusable connection exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One destination parse per CONNECT and socket creation according to the existing pooling/setup behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Named regexp captures `host` and `port` were read using bracket notation with identical values.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Destination parsing and connection establishment precede proxy progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Incoming request/CONNECT count and distinct host:port pool keys; unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Incoming requests retain existing server concurrency and shared-agent limits.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing shared http.Agent continues to pool sockets; no cache or pool key changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all changed identifiers map to the exact same object keys.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Traffic volume varies, but the changed accesses are constant-time equivalents and do not affect socket cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; no repeated parsing, extra connection, allocation growth, or pooling change is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Web page loading and content extraction
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A hidden BrowserWindow loads one main page and its permitted subresources; onBeforeSendHeaders synchronously copies and adjusts headers for every request before it can be sent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the main document and page-generated subresources in Electron.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One main navigation plus site-dependent subresources per extraction, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: DNT and Accept were assigned to the same request-header keys using bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The header callback is on each request's send path, while network loads gate extraction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of subresources requested by the loaded page; unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Electron's existing request scheduling is unchanged; the callback still performs one shallow header copy per request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each loader uses an isolated generated session partition as before; no cache policy or key changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: dot and bracket assignments are semantically equivalent for `DNT` and `Accept`.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Page subresource counts vary, but no additional per-request work is added.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; network fan-out and synchronous request-hook work are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench restore and remote start entry registration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At LifecyclePhase.Restored the contribution reads product configuration, registers actions/listeners, and asynchronously queries installed extensions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing getInstalled call per contribution construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same tunnel configuration object was selected before constructing and initializing the contribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The async query controls the context key but is not newly added or newly awaited by startup due to this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed extension count for the existing find scan; unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The fire-and-forget initialization and listener behavior remain unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache keys or lifecycle changed; product configuration lookup is equivalent.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: `remoteExtensionTips?.tunnel` and bracket access select the same property.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed extension count varies, but the diff does not increase scans or calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; startup work and boundary count remain identical.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remote tunnel contribution command-path unit tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Two tests now construct a local TestInstantiationService and invoke the already-registered public command handler, which immediately traverses mocked dialog/storage/authentication/tunnel services.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly two changed tests; all service implementations on the path are local mocks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tests await one command invocation each and remain serial within their existing suite semantics.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each test uses in-memory storage; no external cache or persisted state is accessed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed setup and invocation occur only in the test file, and transitive services are mocked.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Local test-runner overhead is small and bounded; there is no product-runtime reachability.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable product performance regression; added DI/command-dispatch work is bounded to two tests and crosses no expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and every diff hunk. Production changes are equivalent dot-notation rewrites with unchanged execution frequency, allocation, cache behavior, concurrency, and subprocess/IPC/filesystem/network cardinality. The only structural change is a bounded public-command test seam using mocks. No actionable performance finding or regression-fix learning record was warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
